newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas firms next winter, trades as far as Q3 9.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas firms next winter, trades as far as Q3 9.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices continued to firm in the winter on Friday, traders and brokers said, although prices peaked towards the end of the afternoon and several periods were later offered at or below levels where trade had been done.

The bulk of interest was in the fourth quarter, with at least five trades done between 12.65 pence and 12.725 pence. Several players also said that trade was done in the first quarter at 16.50 pence more than once. But this was not confirmed, and at least one player was sceptical, saying that he had been offering both 16.55 pence and 16.50 pence and had no takers.
The gas year traded several times at up to 12.80 pence, also an increase on the day. Some players believe it is set to get still stronger.

"It's stronger than it was but I still wouldn't say it's particularly strong. We're still only talking about a 12.80 gas year - the normal band is between 12.50 and 13.50, so we're still at the bottom of the band," said one.
He added that there was still quite a lot of buying interest, keeping levels firm.

Trade extended as far out as the third quarter of 1999, which was done at 10.80 pence a therm. By comparison, the third quarter next year was done at 10.30 pence, while the remaining months in 3Q 97, August and September, were done as low as 9.375 pence and 9.60 pence respectively. Dealers cite the Interconnector, due to open in October 1998, as the reason for the higher price in 1999.
One of the largest players in the market was said to have taken several participants to Henley, and the whole market was noticeably less busy than usual even as prices climbed.
IPE futures were firmer in line with the OTC market but only 50 lots were traded in two deals with November trading and settling at 12.70 pence while April traded at 11.90 pence.
